Republic of the Fhilippines DEPARTM OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL VERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, QUEZON CITY ww•.v .dilg.gov. ph BIVAHENG PINOY NA PAUKAD, VAR-AD OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT 22 APR 2014 DILG Legal opinion No. 13, S. 2014 ATTY. LEILENE MARIE C. GALLARDO Director IV National Commission on Indigenous Peoples 2nd Flr., N. dela Merced Bldg., Corner West and Quezon Aves. Quezon City Dear Atty. Gallardo: This has reference to your letter requesting the Department's opinion on whether an Indigenous People (IP) who ran and lost in the recent national elections and was subsequently selected as an IP Mandatory Representative is or is not covered by the prohibition under Section 6, Article IX-B of the 1987 Constitution, which states: "No candidate who has lost in any election, shall within one year after such election, be appointed to any office in the Government or any government-owned or controlled corporations or in any of its subsidiaries. Before we answer your query, may we, at the outset, discuss certain principles. Well-settled is the rule that a person acquires public office either by appointment or by election. An appointment is the act or designation by the executive officer, board or body to where that power has been delegated, of the individual who is to exercise the functions of a given office'. On the other hand, an election "means the choice or selection of candidates to public office by popular vote through the use of the ballot, and the elected officials are determined through the will of the An election is the embodiment of the popular will, the expression of the sovereign power of the people. As you already cited, the 1987 Constitution prohibits the appointment of a losing candidate, within one after such election, to any office in the government or any government-owned or controlled corporations or in any of its subsidiaries. The foregoing Constitutional provision is reiterated under Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 and pertinent CSC issuances, thus: I Mechem, Section 102. 2 Rulloda vs. COMELEC, G.R. No. 154198, 20 January 2003).

Section 94, Republic Act No. 7160 (Local Government Code of 1991) "SECTION 94. Appointment of Elective and Appointive Local Officials; Candidate Who Lost in an Election.—xxx (b) Except for losing candidates in barangay elections, no candidate who lost in any election shall, within one (I) year after such election, be appointed to any office in the Government or any government- owned or-controlled corporations or in any of their subsidiaries. " Section 4, RuleMII, Omnibus Rules on Appointment and Other Personnel Action (CSC Memorandum Circular No. 40, s. 1998, as amended) "Section 4. A person who lost in an election (except Barangay election) shall not be eligible for appointment or reemployment to any office in the government or any government-owned or controlled corporation within one year following such election. " The rationale behind this prohibition is the extirpation of the "spoils system," considering that the foregoing provisions are directed against the so-called "political lameducks"3. Then came Republic Act No. 8371 or the Indigenous People's Rights Act of 1997, which was approved and signed into law on 29 October 1997. Said law provides that the Indigenous Cultural Communities/lndigenous Peoples (ICCs/IPs) have the right to participate fully, if they so choose, at all levels of decision-making in matters which may affect their rights, lives and destinies through procedures determined by them as well as to maintain and develop their own indigenous political structures. Said law recognizes the policy of the State in affording the indigenous people communities adequate representations in the local sanggunians at all levels. On 28 October 2009, the NCIP issued NCIP Administrative Order No. 001, series of 2009 prescribing national guidelines for the mandatory representation of indigenous peoples in the local sanggunians. Section 12 thereof provides and we quote: "SECTION 12. Selection and Assumption to Office. The selection of the particular ICC/IP representative to the local legislative council shall be in accordance with the Local Guideline that the concerned ICCs/IPs shall adopt and promulgate, which considers the cycle of traditional or local activities, and must be compliant to this Administrative Older by containing, at least, the following: a. Title; b. Definitions of Terms; 3 CSC Resolution No. 02-0012, Gato, Vicente S.

c. d. e. g. h. i. j. Selection process which should make a delineation of representation to the levels of Barangay, Municipality, City and Province; Qualifications and Disqualifications; Community Confirmation and Nomination; Vacancy; Disciplinary A ction; Term of Office; Recall/RemovaI; Special Provisions, if any; Amendment; and Effectivity Cla use. For the purpose of ensuring uniformity in the form of the Local Guidelines to be adopted by the concerned ICCs/IPs, the Office of Empowerment and Human Rights (OEHR) shall develop and make available a guide form. Assumption to Office shall take place as soon as the is formally certified by the concerned NCIP Regional Director, upon recommendation of the Provincial or Community Service Center head, as the case may be, to be in accordance with this Administrative Order, and the person chosen takes the appropriate oath before authorized officer and informs the appropriate body/ies of his/her assumption. (Emphasis Supplied) As could be gleaned from the foregoing, RA 8371 and NCIP Administrative Order No. 001, series of 2009 used another term, that is, selection vis-å-vis the representative of ICCs/IPs in the local sanggunians. The next issue therefore is how we would categorize "selection", the mode in which the ICC/IP representative is chosen, is it within the term "election" so that the ICC/IP representative shall be considered as an elective official, or within the term "appointment" so that the IP/ICC representative is an appointed official, thus within the proscription under Section 6, Article IX-B of the 1987 Constitution as reiterated under Section 94 of RA 7160 and Section 4, Rule XIII, Omnibus Rules on Appointment and Other Personnel Action (CSC Memorandum Circular No. 40, s. 1998, as amended)? The Department is of the view that the position of ICC/IP representative is necessarily elective in nature, thus, not within the prohibition under the Constitution, RA 7160 and CSC issuance for the following reasons: 1. As already defined above, an appointment is the act or designation by the executive officer, board or body to where that power has been delegated, of the individual who is to exercise the functions of a given office. May it be respectfully noted that it is not the NCIP or this Department which selects the ICC/IP representative. Under the aforequoted Section 12 of NCIP AO No. 001, series of 2009, the ICCs/IPs themselves chose the particular ICC/IP representative to the local sanggunian in accordance with their Local Guideline

that they themselves have adopted or promulgated for the purpose. The only participation of the NCIP in the process is the issuance, thru their Regional Office, ofa Certificate of Affirmation (COA) to the chosen ICC/IP representative and on the basis of such confirmation, this Department shall thereafter accord due recognition to him/her4. 2. This Department has been consistent in its opinion that it is not the mode to which one acquired office that determines the nature and character of such office. It is the function or role of said office that is controlling. Our classic example is the case of two (2) incumbent regular sanggunian members who were appointed therein to fill the permanent vacancies in the aforesaid August Body. While it may be true that they acquired their positions thru appointment, they should not be considered as appointive members of the sanggunian. The nature and character of the office of the regular member of the sanggunian is elective, the assumption to which, while generally determined by an election, is not precluded by appointment to fill the permanent vacancies that may arise therein. RA 8371 mandates the representation of ICCs/IPs in the local sanggunians at all levels. Such IP/ICC representative shall represent the ICCs/IPs at all levels of decision-making in matters which may affect their rights, lives and destinies through procedures determined by them and in doing so, the ICC/IP representative necessarily will propose in the local sanggunian legislative measures (i.e. ordinance/resolution) towards developing ICC/IP conditions and participate in the deliberations thereof. In fact, in DILG Opinion No. 20, series of 2011, the ICC/IP representative was referred as "ex-officio member of the local sanggunian", the same term that we use to refer to the president of the liga ng mga barangay and sangguniang kabataan from municipal to provincial levels; 3. Lastly, Section 6, Rule IV of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 8371 as reiterated under Section 13 of NCIP AO No. 001, series of 2009, categorically states that the ICC/IP representative shall have and other emoluments as the regular members of the legislative bodies and/or policy making bodies. Based on the foregoing and in reply to your query, we are of the view the position of ICC/IP representative is necessarily elective in nature thus, not within the purview of the aforequoted prohibition under the 1987 Constitution, RA 7160 and CSC issuance. On a final note, the foregoing opinion however does not preclude you or other concerned party/ies from seeking a more authoritative opinion from the Department of Justice since the issue posed involves a legal issue. The foregoing initial opinion was rendered since you cited a similar provision of the Local Government Code of 1991, the law which this Department is primarily tasked to interpret. Section 16, NCIP AO No. 001, series of2009.

We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. V t ly yours, Isil 7 Copy furnished: RD JOHN M. CASTANEDA Barangay Center, Upper Session Road Baguio City AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary DILG-OUSLG
